    A Date survives a remote call
    
    Date.prototype.toJSON produces a bare string, so a Date that crosses the wire
    arrived as text and every z.date() on the far side rejected it -- ZodError:
    Invalid date, on a response that was correct when it was sent. Every collection
    has createdAt/updatedAt, so this broke every remote read of every collection
    while the suite stayed green, because a local call never serializes.
    
    Revival rather than a tagged envelope, deliberately. Tagging is more precise and
    changes the wire format, so a new node and an old node would disagree in both
    directions during a rolling upgrade. Reviving leaves the bytes unchanged: each
    reads the other correctly, and seven machines can be upgraded one at a time.
    
    The cost is stated in the code rather than discovered later: a z.string() field
    holding a full ISO instant becomes a Date and fails its own schema. The pattern
    is anchored and demands the T, the time and a zone, so a plain date is untouched.
    
    Finishes item 3 of surfdns#43, which ran out of quota mid-change.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
